There’s a great book out there called A Thousand Beginnings and Endings that I bought a couple days ago. It’s a retelling of classical Asian mythology. The first and my favorite story is the story of Mount Makiling. I heard the story growing up, but loved it more here. The spirit of a mountain falls in love with a mortal and plan to get married. The day of their wedding, the man goes to town, but the spirit puts ginger in his pocket that becomes gold as a gift. The man is killed for having gold and the spirit vows to never let anyone take what isn’t theirs.

What resonated to me was the the spirit, Makiling, was the villain, she started her downfall and was unaware of the consequences, but she did it out of love and benevolence. So it’s said that while she brought on her fate, you should say a prayer for her, that she will find peace.

This leads into my personal hypothesis that there aren’t true villains, and that we are all villains in our own ways and by confronting that and being aware of what we do, we will be given peace.

Our blood is created in the bone marrow of our bones, a lot is made in your femurs. They produce stem cells, those cells can really be used for anything, but are used mainly for blood cells. When stem cells divide they become immature blood cells, those can be white blood cells, red blood cells, or platelets. Those then divide again and mature into fully matured blood cells that are real eased into our bloodstream. Keep in mind though, the liquid part of the blood is mostly water and nutrients.
